extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs), and NIH staff involved in extramural peer review
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: High-level policy and issue guidance for the initial peer review of NIH extramural grant applications, including who manages reviews, the review objective, and oversight functions to assure review quality and appropriate expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of initial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial review is to rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial reviews are carried out by peer review groups composed of scientists from the extramural research community; scoring should focus on scientific and technical merit as the central evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of initial review groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for support from the NIH are reviewed initially by peer review groups composed of scientists from the extramural research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer panels should be drawn from appropriate extramural scientific expertise to evaluate the merit of proposals; reviewer selection and rosters are provided as CSR resources (Study Section Rosters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of the initial review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial review process is managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRAs are responsible for administrating the review meeting/process logistics and ensuring review criteria and procedures are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: OER responsibility for peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Extramural Research (OER) manages the development and implementation of policies and procedures that pertain to peer review conducted in all components of the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER sets overarching policy and procedural standards that guide how peer review is conducted across NIH components.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR role for investigator-initiated applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Scientific Review (CSR) manages the initial review groups that review most of the investigator-initiated applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR handles the bulk of initial peer review for unsolicited investigator-initiated submissions; CSR resources include Study Section Rosters and Review and Referral guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICs role for special solicitations and unique programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The awarding institutes and centers (ICs) manage the review of applications submitted in response to special solicitations and for unique programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applications respond to institute/center-specific solicitations or unique program needs, the relevant IC assumes responsibility for managing review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Oversight and policy advice (PROG function)
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of the Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) is to advise and make recommendations on the development and implementation of policies pertaining to the monitoring of, coordination of, and evaluation of peer review conducted at the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROG advises NIH leadership to ensure review processes keep pace with current advances in research and that peer reviewer expertise is appropriate for the needs of science; PROG issues meeting minutes, agendas, and rosters documenting deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reviewer expertise is appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review must ensure that the peer reviewer expertise is appropriate for the needs of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of oversight and policy, mechanisms should be in place to match reviewer expertise to applications and to update reviewer pools as scientific fields evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, coordination, and evaluation of peer review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies should address monitoring, coordination, and evaluation of peer review conducted at the NIH to keep processes aligned with advances in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing evaluation and coordination across components (CSR, ICs, OER) is required to maintain fairness, timeliness, and relevance of review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explicit statements of review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Announces New Explicit Statements of Review Criteria (reference to policy document emphasizing explicit criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and policy documents (e.g., 'Rating of Grant Applications') provide explicit review criteria that reviewers and applicants should follow; these documents are part of the peer review policy resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of public representatives/participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of Public Representatives/Participants in Scientific Peer Review (identified as a topic/issue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH tracks and provides guidance on the role and inclusion of public representatives in peer review, indicating inclusion considerations are part of peer review policy discussions.
